descs.t: Russia has agreed to resume three-way talks on the Ukraine war with Kyiv and Washington, the Kremlin says. The announcement comes as Ukraine reports three waves of ballistic missiles fired at Kyiv. We walk through what was agreed, what happened overnight and what each side is saying.

The Kremlin says Russia will return to three-way Ukraine talks with Kyiv and Washington, while Zelensky says 21 missiles were fired at Kyiv since the previous evening. US envoy Steve Witkoff thanked Putin for being a humanitarian. We look at who gains from these talks and what they mean for Washington.

Russia says it wants peace talks with Kyiv and Washington, yet Ukraine says Kyiv was targeted by three waves of ballistic missiles. At the same time a US envoy praised Putin as a humanitarian. We lay out why talks under fire should worry everyone who wants a real peace.

intro.plain: The Kremlin says Russia will resume three-way talks on the Ukraine war with Kyiv and Washington. At the same time, Zelensky says three waves of ballistic missiles, 21 in total, were fired at Kyiv since yesterday evening. So talks are back on paper, but the strikes have not stopped. Tell me in the chat: do you think these talks lead anywhere real?
intro.mid: Russia says yes to three-way talks with Kyiv and Washington, and almost in the same breath fires 21 ballistic missiles at Kyiv, by Zelensky's count. Meanwhile US envoy Steve Witkoff thanked Putin for being a humanitarian. Question for the chat: is Washington being too soft on Putin right now?
intro.bold: Putin wants a seat at the peace table and he wants to keep hitting Kyiv. Ukraine says 21 ballistic missiles came in three waves. And an American envoy called Putin a humanitarian. Chat, be honest: should the US push harder on Moscow before any talks?

hook.plain: Russia says it will return to three-way talks with Kyiv and Washington. Ukraine says 21 ballistic missiles were fired at Kyiv. Here is what was agreed and what it means.
hook.mid: Peace talks back on, missiles still flying. Zelensky counts 21 fired at Kyiv while the Kremlin agrees to talks. Here is who gains and who loses.
hook.bold: Ukraine says three waves of ballistic missiles were fired at Kyiv, and a US envoy calls Putin a humanitarian. This is what talks under fire really look like.

descs.t: Stella Parton, Dolly Parton's sister, says a Tennessee voting machine repeatedly switched her selection to Republican Marsha Blackburn. Her claim spread fast as early voting got underway in several states, alongside other posts reporting machines changing votes. We walk through exactly what she says happened and what is still unconfirmed.

Dolly Parton's sister Stella Parton says her Tennessee voting machine kept switching her pick to Marsha Blackburn. Her account landed in the middle of early voting, with some accounts already calling it evidence of rigging. We separate her claim from the conclusions people are drawing from it, and look at what voters can check before they cast a ballot.

Stella Parton says a Tennessee voting machine kept overriding her choice and handing it to Republican Marsha Blackburn. With early voting underway and accounts on both the left and the right already talking about stolen votes, one famous name's claim can move a lot of people. We look at what she actually said, what is proven, and what every voter should do at the machine.

intro.plain: Big story out of Tennessee. Stella Parton, Dolly Parton's sister, says a voting machine repeatedly switched her selection to Republican Marsha Blackburn. That is her claim, and it is spreading fast while early voting is underway in several states. I want to go through what she says happened and what is still unconfirmed. Chat, if you voted early on a machine, did you check your ballot before casting it?
intro.mid: Dolly Parton's sister just became the face of a voting machine fight. Stella Parton says her machine in Tennessee kept switching her choice to Marsha Blackburn. Some accounts are already calling it proof the election is being rigged. A claim is not proof, so let's look at what she actually said and what it would take to show it. Chat, do you trust the machine in your precinct?
intro.bold: Imagine pressing your choice and watching the screen hand it to someone else. That is what Stella Parton, Dolly Parton's sister, says happened to her in Tennessee, over and over, with the vote going to Marsha Blackburn. Early voting is underway and this is exactly the kind of story that shakes trust. So what is proven here? Chat, has a machine ever done this to you?

hook.bold: She says she picked one name and the machine kept picking Marsha Blackburn. Stella Parton's claim is now everywhere in early voting. Here is what it means for every voter standing at a screen.
